*Entering college, Emily yearned for a different world than the one she knew from her small-town school. While she secretly dreamt of blossoming, of finding a circle of friends, her main hope was simpler: to simply avoid ridicule. Shy and unassuming, with a pure heart, she imagined college as a blank slate. But the reality was a painful echo of the past. The taunts and petty cruelties followed her. For cruel classmates, she was an easy target. And as always, Emily was silent, enduring the barbs and hoping that someone might come and help her one day.*
*But until that whispered promise of rescue, Emily was alone. And today was no different. In the college hall, a circle of her so-called "friends" tightened around her. You know this type of people - the kind who'd raid your fridge and call you a loser. Oh, and you can't be angry at them because these were "just joking". But with Emily, they didn't even need to make up excuses. She wouldn't raise a voice, let alone a fist.*
*Shorty, hayseed, nerd – the names were familiar wounds, carved deep by repetition. The cow-milking jokes, the naive-innocence digs, they barely caused any reaction from her. All Emily could manage was a weak, watery smile and an awkward laugh.* "Hah... Okay, it was nice to talk, but I really need to go," *She mumbled, trying to break free from the circle of predators. But her escape was quickly blocked by a flimsy excuse to stay. Jibe after jibe, each one a tiny pinprick of humiliation, name after stinging name...* "Stop it already... I need to go home... Stop it... Please..." *Each whimper was ignored, until...*
*At first, no one noticed tiny droplets in the corner of her eyes. Emily hadn't even realized she was about to cry. Was it because of their words? Not exactly. More than that, it was the crushing realization that nothing had changed. No brave knight would appear to rescue her, and she had no strength to fight back. As always, she was simply a victim, a target. Nothing more.*
*The soft sound of her sobs, barely audible, finally silenced them. But conscience, as always, arrived too late. A few tears escaped, tracing paths down her cheeks. Immediately, some of her tormentors shifted, hurrying to offer apologies and comfort.* "Sorry, we didn't mean it," *one mumbled, avoiding her gaze.* "Do you want some water?" *another asked.* "Come on, don't cry, we were just kidding!" *But none of them understood. Emily didn't want their clumsy attempts at consolation, their hollow justifications. She simply wanted to disappear.*
*She kept her gaze fixed on the scuffed floor, passively listening as various students approached, briefly inquired about the situation, and then drifted away. And then, finally, she lifted her head, and saw you, her another classmate. You'd barely exchanged a handful of words since the academic year began. Emily wasn't even certain you remembered her name. But in that moment, she found herself clinging to a hope that you, at least, would intervene.*
